verdict.tagline: Messy management and brutal police make a compelling, flawed empire.
for_you_if: you enjoy building complex automated production chains
you can laugh off sudden multiplayer crashes
you want deep management systems to master
not_for_you_if: you expect a polished endgame without repetition
you lose patience with progress-deleting bugs
you need balanced police difficulty on release

claims.claim: Handler NPCs bug out by depositing items onto storage slots with a locked symbol, deleting the products.

citations.review_text: Game started off fairly fun. Once I got access to Helpers, the game went downhill fast. The Handler NPC frequently bugs when moving product from the Packaging Station to a Storage Rack. One or more of the storage slots gets a Locked symbol yet the Handler NPC will continue to deposit packaged weed onto it, effectively deleting the drugs. I can make $10k per day easily by doing my own packaging, but I'm broke when using the Handler NPC because it bugs so frequently.

👍 Recommended... with reservations

I had fun with Schedule I for about 12 hours. The early game is addictive, progression feels rewarding, and building your operation from nothing is genuinely entertaining. For $20, I don't feel like I got ripped off.

The problem starts once your business gets bigger.

Instead of feeling like you're running an empire, it turns into constant micromanagement. You're always refilling stash houses, restocking supplies, checking inventory, and handling repetitive tasks that should eventually be automated. Expanding your operation doesn't make you feel more powerful—it just creates more chores.

The game desperately needs better late-game automation. An inventory manager, automatic restocking, supply routes, or employees who can manage stock without constant player input would make a huge difference. Right now, growth feels like a punishment instead of a reward.

Overall, I enjoyed my time with it and think there's a great game here. The foundation is solid, but the late game needs more quality-of-life features to keep it fun instead of turning into busywork.

Worth $20? I'd say yes, but mostly because the first 10–15 hours are enjoyable. I just hope future updates focus on making the late game less tedious.

I want to like it, but once you get to a certain, fairly early point the game becomes less "build your shady drug empire" and more "figure out the annoying details of how to assign roles to NPCs to automate blending weed with bananas, donuts, gas station boner pills, horse semen, and gasoline"

claims.claim: Reviewers find that the gameplay becomes repetitive and lacks sufficient content or storyline once reaching the end game.

citations.review_text: After the benzies part it gets a bit boring, i stopped playing it because it didn't have a big enough story and got a little boring overtime.

The community votes are pointless.

The game needs more polishing and improvements to features that have already been implemented. I don't care about new customers—right now it feels pointless because the gameplay is still the same repetitive cycle. I can stack all my deliveries after midnight and finish them at the 4 AM mark, which completely freezes the game... WHY?! It's incredibly stupid.

The police need improvements, gangs need improvements, and THE MAP NEEDS TO BE BIGGER!! There are many other issues that should be addressed before adding more content.

The game also needs more side activities besides the casino. Even after the nerf, the casino is still overpowered and can make an insane amount of money. There should be more profitable and engaging alternatives so players aren't forced to rely on the casino as the best way to earn cash.

I bought this game on day one, so I know what I'm talking about. This is Unity, not Unreal Engine. Stop pretending the engine is the reason basic gameplay improvements are taking so long.

I don't want to hate on the game, but I'm tired of all the unnecessary glazing. The game is still way too easy, and it WILL STILL be easy after the customers update if nothing else changes.

That being said, I still think the game is fun and has a lot of potential. The biggest issue isn't that the game is bad—it's that the gameplay becomes repetitive after a while. Discovering new drug combinations and seeing all the hilarious effects they create is one of the most enjoyable parts of the game. The humor is one of its strongest features and keeps the experience entertaining.

Even though the casino is overpowered and needs better balancing, it is still a fun activity. The problem is that there aren't enough other activities that are just as enjoyable and rewarding. More variety would help keep the gameplay fresh and give players more reasons to continue playing.

I bought this game because I saw its potential, and I still believe it can beco…

At first this game was really good but it’s been lacking ever since it’s blow up. I’ve got a pretty good amount of hours and once u reach like endgame there’s not much to work to/for or even do without it being very repetitive. 
And I believe blaming it on Early Access is a weak excuse. This game had more than enough players and resources at its peak to scale up and pump out quality updates.
When you release a game in Early Access, the expectation is that you're actively working with the community to make it better. Instead, we get constant delays on things that were already scheduled and announced—if we get them at all.
This game could have achieved so much more if Tyler actually wanted it to. He doesn’t have to do this entirely alone; he chooses to. If you're going to use the 'Early Access' label as a shield, you should actually be creating and dropping the updates on time. Is asking for a schedule to be kept really that crazy? Lol.
I’ve even mentioned this in the official discord and got corny, dismissive, and sarcastic responses from admins like “good for you buddy” then was muted for calling them out on it lol. It just says a lot about this game and its future without saying anything at all. They had nothing else to say other than resorting to that behavior because they know what I said is true everything is lagging and they can’t defend the management so they resort to the “too cool to care act” and getting their little feelings because his little bit of internet power was challenged. So they had to pull the natural discord mod move to get the last word. Obviously I just left the discord after because again it says a lot about the management without saying anything at all. This kind of toxic management is exactly how communities die out, along with the game itself. So I mean it was good but would I recommend this game after the first 3 months since its release,  probably not.

Buen juego pero muy repetitivo, con mods es una locura. Deben meter mas cosas o historia.
Graficos:8/10
Gameplay:7/10
Si te lo quieres comprar, hazlo no te vas a aburrir al principio pero a medida que avanzas se vuelve repetitivo.

Honestly, I usually hate simulator style games and never really get into them. But this is the one game that actually made one of my DREAMS come true. The progression, the grind, and the feeling of building your own empire kept me hooked for hours.

I’m really looking forward to the next update. I hope the developers add new quests, storylines, territories, challenges, and more content to keep the game fresh. I’ve already wiped out the Benzies, so things are starting to feel a little repetitive without new thrills or action packed objectives.

That said, this game has completely taken over my free time in the best way possible. Salute Devs!

I looked into it and it appears to be certain mixes in the products.json are not in the registry in the latest update and it's caused issues with my saved game. So many hours put in just wasted. I reported it in the bug reports discussion section with technical info, but nothing has been updated.

My other reason for not recommending is not because I don't think the game is fun and a great idea, but because it now feels totally abandoned, no updates since like maybe January (i forget exactly when last) and those updates contained no bug fixes that helped and just seemed to offer very little extra to the game.

If updates start coming and the game gets built on along with bug fixes for all the issues, i'll maybe revisit my review. I would have thought with all the revenue generated from this game that there would be a team of devs behind it now building on what was already a great foundations, unfortunately for whatever reason that hasn't happened. Great potential, but sadly not capitalised on. Oh well, it was fun while it lasted.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that managing employees, handlers, and automated workers can be tedious and requires intensive planning.

citations.review_text: I have to force myself to stay away from this game so I don't get burnt out on it, especially when I know a new update is afoot. I love this game an unreasonable amount. Of course, this game is incredibly fun at face value, the customization elements, stealthing through the map, and the sandbox style of how you run your operation are enthralling and entertaining long term. The artstyle is charming and low enough on graphic fidelity that, while I now play on my new Gaming Computer, when I was running this game on my ♥♥♥♥♥♥ college laptop it much smoother than most of the games I'd run (ie. Lollipop Chainsaw, The Binding of Isaac, ♥♥♥♥, even PlateUp or South Park The Fractured But Whole would get powerpoint-esque). I also greatly enjoy the replay value of the game, especially since the introduction of seeded mixing -- mixing is perhaps the most customizable and fun parts of the game, and my friend group often fights over the role when we play together. The feeling of a new exploration with each playthrough is a godsend for the longevity of the game. My one critique as of now would be that the game can become grindy, especially when you employ NPCs. The process of programming each employee and jumping through some hoops to ensure it runs akin to a well oiled machine is tedious, and I often take breaks from the game for a few hours or the rest of the day because of the intensive planning required for this mechanic to be utilized effectively. That being said, I think the game is remarkably in depth and polished for its current state of development, and even if the team quit working on the project altogether I would maintain a conviction that my purchase of this game has been money well spent. While more enjoyable with friends, the singleplayer experience is nothing to sneeze at in any way shape or form, and most of my hours have been spent in the latter mode of play. To compare the two is similar to comparing ice cream or cake, I find. If you haven't picked this game up …

I just cant anymore, I've tried playing several times over the last several months. Its always fun in the beginning, screwing around becoming the local drug dealer king pin. That novelty falls off and your left trying to optimize your farms and workers and managing inventory non-stop. The delivery updates were huge, but the fact I still cant make workers unload vans is crazy work. Janitors are useless, why cant my botanist clean up after themselves just like chemist do? Its an unnecessary management obstacle. Speaking of management, it needs reworked from the core. I should be able to rename storage shelfs and mixing stations, that alone would make management SOOO much easier. Also what should be included is an actual interface so you can SEE if you made any mistakes / find them as they occur. One last thing, dear god fix the disappearing inventory! Im so sick of working the endgame for 12-15 stacks of my premium product to disappear completely from the game.

I have 250 hours in this game. But I am not going to play it anymore until I see one change implemented. If we have several storage racks or closets stacked up together, (touching) we should be able to define any number of those racks as "one". I waste wayyyyy too much handler moving routes just trying to keep a single shelf stocked with the several stocked shelves next to it. PLEASE MAKE THIS CHANGE! It's a massive limitation in my ability to have my staff keep things going. Another thing that would be nice and frankly make sense is for the chemists to have a definable supply rack just as the botanists do. So again we don't have to use handler's to keep the mixers and meth stations stocked. It just makes more sense. For the love of God! Please do it!! OH AND ONE MORE THING!!! When I have a handler unload a delivery van, the handler has (if i remember correctly) 5 slots to carry items on them... but they only use one slot when unloading delivery vans. This results in a painfully slow process of them unloading vans and just screws up efficiency to a point where it's not even a functional option.
